skill.author: andreadellacorte

security_audit.summary: The static detections are Markdown references or constrained project setup operations, with no user-controlled command construction or data exfiltration. However, the skill directs agents to execute mutable remote installation instructions and grants broad command scopes, creating supply-chain and indirect prompt-injection exposure.

remediation.issue: The skill requires agents to read remote installation pages and run their current instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace remote instruction execution with reviewed, version-pinned commands for each supported platform, and require user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: The allowed tool declaration permits unrestricted npx and broad CLI subcommands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove npx unless required, narrow command permissions to documented subcommands, and request confirmation before any network-backed package execution.

content.user_title: Install and Configure a Task Backend
content.value_statement: Task backends require separate CLI installation, verification, and project configuration. This skill guides setup for beans, Linear, GitHub, or disabled task storage.
actual_capabilities: Reads the configured task storage backend from the Groove project configuration.
Stops without installation when task storage is set to none.
Checks whether the selected backend CLI is installed and reachable.
Initializes beans storage and derives a project prefix from repository information.
Places beans task files under the project-local Groove directory.
limitations: Supports only beans, the third-party Linear CLI, GitHub CLI, or no backend.
Depends on remote upstream installation instructions when a required CLI is missing.
Requires shell, network, and project filesystem access for installation and configuration.
Does not configure hosted service credentials or guarantee successful authentication.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Groove Project
use_cases.description: Install the selected task CLI, verify availability, and create the initial project configuration.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Task Storage
use_cases.description: Configure beans task paths and prefixes consistently across a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Repair an Incomplete Backend Setup
use_cases.description: Check the configured backend, restore missing beans configuration, and report the resulting storage path.
use_cases.target_user: DevOps engineers troubleshooting local project setup

prompt_templates.title: Check Task Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this project's task storage setting. Tell me which backend is selected and whether its CLI is available. Do not install anything.

prompt_templates.title: Install Configured Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up the task backend configured for this Groove project. Confirm before installing software, then report the installed version and changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Beans Storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure beans for this repository. Derive a concise project prefix, place tasks under the Groove directory, and verify the final configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Repair Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current task backend setup. Preserve valid configuration, identify missing dependencies, propose changes, and apply only approved installation or migration steps.

output_examples.input: Check the configured task backend without changing the repository.
output_examples.output: Task storage is disabled. No CLI installation or project changes are required.

output_examples.input: Initialize beans for this repository and summarize the result.
output_examples.output: Beans storage was initialized under the Groove tasks directory. The project prefix was derived from the repository name, and the CLI check succeeded.
GitHub CLI is available. The response reports its version and authentication status without changing task storage files.

best_practices: Review installation commands and confirm package sources before allowing execution.
Commit project configuration changes so task storage conventions remain consistent for the team.
Verify the selected CLI version and resulting storage path after setup.
anti_patterns: Do not execute mutable remote instructions without reviewing the exact commands.
Do not overwrite an existing beans configuration without inspecting its current values.
Do not move task data until the destination exists and repository status is checked.

faq.question: Which task backends are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports beans, a third-party Linear CLI, GitHub CLI, and a disabled storage option.

faq.question: What happens when task storage is disabled?
faq.answer: The skill reports that no setup is needed and exits without installing a CLI.

faq.question: Does the skill install missing software?
faq.answer: Yes. It can follow upstream installation guidance for the selected CLI, which requires network and shell access.

faq.question: How is the beans project prefix chosen?
faq.answer: It derives an uppercase abbreviation from the repository name and falls back to the current directory name.

faq.question: Where are beans task files stored?
faq.answer: The generated configuration places task files in the project-local Groove tasks directory.

faq.question: Does the skill authenticate hosted services?
faq.answer: No. It can check CLI authentication status, but credentials and hosted service access remain the user's responsibility.
